summary: The iOS app's chat feed shows a row for five runtime events it used to drop, with the same identity and copy as native Android: turn.retrying (Retrying with a spinner, Retry finished once the turn ends or the session leaves running, one row per turn), worktree.drift (Worktree changed with the branch and path, one row per chat updated in place), spend.blocked (Spend blocked with instance and model, reason, scope and reset time, one row per instance and model), peer.message (Received or Sent with the other chat's name, the text, and who sent it) and todo.updated (the agent's checklist, replaced by its id). The rows are read-only on both phones. A peer row uses the id of the row the backend stores (h-<messageId> for a received message, h-peer_<messageId> for a sent one), so a history merge lands on the live row. A full reload shows the stored rows: the received message as a user bubble and the sent one as a Sent to notice, the same as Android. Retry, drift, spend and todo rows are not stored by the backend, so a reload does not show them on either phone.

desktop.reason: The desktop already handles these events (provider-event-reducer.ts and the composer's drift and spend warnings). Only the iOS client changes.

sharedBackendApi.reason: No event, field or channel changes. The phone reads the existing turn.retrying, worktree.drift, spend.blocked, peer.message and todo.updated events from src/shared/provider-events.ts and calls no new channel.

storageDataMigration.reason: No backend storage change. The phone's chat cache (sb-chat-cache) stores the new feed kinds as plain JSON beside the existing ones; an older app version that reads such a cache renders nothing for an unknown kind, and the next history load reseeds the feed, so no cache version bump is needed.

updateRelease.reason: JavaScript only, with no native module, permission or app.json change, so the fingerprint runtimeVersion is unchanged and it ships on the mobile-ota.yml iOS lane. Android is unchanged.

automated: npx vitest run tests/unit/mobile-chat-store.test.ts tests/unit/mobile-event-rows.test.ts: retry rows stop on turn.completed and on a status other than running, drift and todo rows update in place, spend rows are one per instance and model, peer rows use the stored row ids and a history merge lands on them, and the copy of each row
npx jest (apps/mobile): EventRowItem renders the retry spinner only while active, the peer heading, text and sender, and one status icon per todo
npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/mobile and npm run typecheck
notExercised: No row was seen on an iPhone or a simulator; a live retry, drift, spend block, peer delivery or todo update was not produced against a running backend.
The rows are read-only on both phones: neither offers the desktop's Follow action for a drift or a model switch for a spend block.
